newsitem.title: CROATIA: First Croatian train rolls into Eastern Slavonia.
newsitem.headline: First Croatian train rolls into Eastern Slavonia.

text.p: The first Croatian train rolled into the last Serb enclave of the country on Tuesday and a commercial bank opened a branch -- both concrete signs that Eastern Slavonia will soon be fully reintegrated into Croatia.

The train, carrying experts of the state railway, pulled up in the enclave's largest town Vukovar after Croatian military engineers completed 50 days of demining and mending the badly damaged line, state television said.
The railway is open for traffic at reduced speed though officials didn't say when passenger traffic would resume.

Eastern Slavonia is now monitored by the United Nations whose current mandate expires on July 15, when Croatia expects to regain full control of the region. It broke away in 1991 when Serbs rebelled against Croatia's secession from Yugoslavia.

Croatian bank Slavonska Banka, based in the nearby city of Osijek, opened a branch in the eastern town of Beli Manastir on the same day -- the first Croatian bank to move into Eastern Slavonia since the country won independence in 1991.
It will start transactions on Wednesday, the state news agency HINA said.

Croatia introduced its currency, the kuna, into the enclave last week when Serbs were allowed to exchange their Yugoslav dinars. Both currencies will be officially accepted in the enclave for the next two months.
